sections.Highlights: THIS... is a 2025 Ferrari SF90 Spider, finished in Bianco Cervino with a Nero interior. The odometer on this SF90 currently displays approximately 182 miles. The attached Carfax history report lists no accidents or mileage discrepancies in this SF90's brief past. According to the window sticker provided in the gallery, notable factory equipment includes carbon ceramic brakes, a front axle lift system, an Adaptive Front-lighting System, Scuderia Ferrari fender shields, a power-retractable hardtop, a carbon fiber steering wheel with LEDs, and Apple CarPlay connectivity. The seller reports no notable modifications. Unveiled in 2019, the SF90 Stradale stood out as Ferrari's first series-produced plug-in hybrid model and its first all-wheel-drive car with a mid-mounted engine. It puts nearly 1,000 horsepower under the driver's right foot, and the extensive use of carbon fiber helped offset the hybrid system's weight. The SF90 was a new kind of Ferrari inside as well: the brand replaced most of the buttons with touch-sensitive surfaces. Production of the SF90 ended in 2024. Power comes from a gasoline-electric plug-in hybrid drivetrain, which consists of a twin-turbocharged 4.0-liter V8, three electric motors, and a 7.9-kilowatt-hour lithium-ion battery pack. The system's total output is rated at a combined 986 horsepower and 590 lb-ft of torque. The V8 and one of the motors spin the rear wheels via an 8-speed dual-clutch automatic transmission, while the front-mounted motors spin one front wheel each.
